## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the front wheels.
2. Cut off or remove rusted lower shock bolts using a sawzall, pneumatic cutting wheel, and spark plugs if necessary.
3. Install new OME shocks with 1/2-inch spacers on top of the tophats.
4. Secure the upper knuckle by locking two nuts together on the tophat studs to allow for tightening.

_Procedure reported by [t559]._

## Tips & gotchas

- Machine the blocks so the machined side faces toward the inside of the truck to clear the seating area slope. [t755]
- [Partial] Ensure all components are lined up before tightening everything down completely. [t755]
- Orient the larger end of the shim facing the front of the truck to tilt the axle housing upward. [t373]
- Stock 2nd gen Xterra rear axle weighs approximately 2120 lbs unloaded. [t558]
- Aim to order springs rated for a load slightly higher than your current loaded weight to prevent excessive settling. [t558]
- The curved center of the SLR bracket provides extra ground clearance in the middle. [t829]
- [Partial] Drop brackets raise suspension travel while keeping front driveline specs within factory limits. [t829]
- Use heavier springs or a spacer at the top to increase load capacity when running higher settings like 0.5 inches. [t553]
- Consider adding extended brake lines and larger bump stops (e.g., Timbren) if using Titan-length coilovers. [t553]
- [Partial] Extend the rear bump stop by the exact amount of lift added with shackles to prevent inverting leaf springs. [t553]
- [Partial] Turn the steering wheel full lock on each side while removing sway bar links to gain working room. [t932]
- [Partial] Clean dirt from threads before installing new hardware, especially if using stock nuts. [t932]
- Lock two nuts together on the top hat studs if standard stud length is insufficient. [t559]
- Check tire well measurements after a week or two. [t559]
- Use an adjustable shackle system for easier installation and adjustment. [t612]
- Slide the bumper onto the threaded anchor bolts before fully tightening them down for alignment. [t612]
- Use extended axle shafts (e.g., from PRG) to accommodate the increased track width caused by Titan control arms. [t881]
- Remove CV joints and replace stock Xterra axle shafts with longer ones if necessary. [t881]
- Use camber bolts to allow for proper alignment after adding spacers. [t895]
- Consider dropping the rear sway bar while working underneath. [t895]
- Add an adjustable shackle to the rear leaf pack instead of a solid Air Assist Leaf (AAL) for adjustability. [t895]
- Note that shackles push the leaf pack down to create lift, while AALs add structural height. [t895]
- [Partial] Use an adjustable shackle set at the middle hole to regain lost height after installing a rear bumper. [t895]
- A single-leaf AAL is considered the worst option for rear suspension. [t895]
- Combining an AAL with a shackle provides added height and compensates for lost wheel travel. [t895]
- You may not strictly need upgraded UCAs if lifting less than 2 inches, but coil bucket contact can still occur. [t895]
- [Partial] Install bump stops on your own UCAs to allow for more travel. [t895]
- A 1.25-inch spacer mounted above a coil spring effectively provides approximately 2 inches of total lift. [t817]
- [Partial] Running spacers higher than 1 inch on adjustable shocks may cause them to top out violently during bumps. [t817]
- [Partial] If using heavy-duty springs with a front bumper, stock height shock settings might be too stiff; consider adjusting the preload down. [t817]
- Stock Xterra leaf springs are undersprung from the factory. [t888]
- Alcan springs offer better ride quality and weight handling than OME for vehicles carrying extra armor. [t888]
- If using heavy aftermarket armor on OME springs without the HD leaf, expect them to flatten out within a year or two. [t888]
- The front suspension components are identical between vehicles. [t253]
- Consult PRG or Nisstec to ensure the upper control arms are matched correctly for your specific spacer height. [t959]
- The AAL helps stiffen the notoriously weak stock leaf pack, preventing sagging under load. [t959]
- [Partial] Use this method if you have already installed large spacers and HD coils without upgrading to coilovers. [t1004]
- [Partial] Allow the vehicle's weight to settle onto the jack stand corner while compressing the spring. [t1004]
- Consider this setup for a balance between on-road and off-road ride quality. [t545]
- [Partial] Note that the leaf pack may sag quickly, though this can be mitigated by removing one or two leaves to soften the ride. [t545]
- Pair with SPC Upper Control Arms (UCAs) if the lift allows the UCA to contact the coil bucket, preventing upper ball joints from pulling apart under down-travel. [t545]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Ordering springs that are too soft (e.g., +450 or +600) if the vehicle is heavily modified with a Titan axle and roof rack. [t558]
- [Partial] Choosing spring lengths over 4 inches which can cause arch issues on short second-gen Xterra leafs. [t558]
- Over-tightening aluminum PRG spacers which can strip the holes. [t932]
- [Partial] Reusing old cotter pins instead of straightening or replacing them. [t932]
- Failing to secure the spindle assembly before removing the upper ball joint nut, causing stress on lines. [t932]
- [Partial] Choosing a non-rebuildable shock if you plan to keep the old ones for later. [t148]
- [Partial] Using universal shock bolts with rubber over metal that don't seat properly. [t559]
- [Partial] Breaking off cotter pins in rusty holes without drilling them out first. [t559]
- Tightening tophat nuts before securing the knuckle, causing the arm to slide down. [t559]
- [Partial] Drilling new holes 2" down on both sides (unless you have the time). [t612]
- [Partial] Following instructions that suggest drilling new lower holes instead of cutting slots from the original top mounts. [t612]
- [Partial] Setting the adjustable Bilstein 5100s higher than 1 inch without accounting for spacer lift can blow out the shocks. [t817]
- [Partial] Ignoring coil bucket contact (CBC) which limits up-travel and creates noise when running spacers over stock UCA's. [t817]
- [Partial] Choosing standard rate springs when running significant added weight like full body armor. [t888]
- Adding heavy components before finalizing suspension specs for load capacity. [t888]
- [Partial] Bottoming out shocks due to limited travel if not balanced with longer shock bodies. [t959]
- [Partial] Boltting up the UCA before fully seating it by compressing the spring enough, leading to constant contact with the coils bucket. [t1004]
